opening_message:
Ticket 1: John Rodriguez (employee ID E049) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E049.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: John Rodriguez (E049) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role, which is Engineer). Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows John Rodriguez (E049) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max; recommend granting read.
reason: There is a conflict between the two notes: HR lists John Rodriguez (E049) as a full-time Analyst, but the Security database lists him as a contractor with basic security training. Under the access policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read access to Source Code (write requires advanced training; admin is never allowed for contractors). Since the requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, the maximum (read) is granted, and nothing above the requested level is granted.
